title: Returning a buffer with a head at or before its end
statement: Let $A$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $r$ be one of its states, and choose one of its work tapes. Suppose that from its initial configuration on input $x$, machine $A$ reaches a configuration $d$ after $a$ steps, with state $r$, empty output, contents of the chosen tape equal to the buffer holding $w$, and head position $j\le |w|$. Assume $A$'s initial state differs from $r$ and every configuration in state $r$ is fixed by one step of $A$. Then the machine obtained by extending $A$ with the output procedure computes $w$ on input $x$ within $a+j+|w|+4$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: $A$ is a finite machine over the Boolean alphabet
A work tape of $A$ is chosen
$d$ is a configuration on input $x$ reached from the initial configuration of $A$ after $a$ steps
every configuration in state $r$ is fixed by one step of $A$
the chosen tape in $d$ contains the buffer for $w$
the chosen tape head in $d$ is at position $j$
replaced: Let a machine reach, in $a$ steps from its native start, an absorbing completion whose chosen tape holds the word $w$ with its head at some position $j \le |w|$, with empty output and a start control distinct from the completion. Then the replay-extended machine computes $w$ from the same input within $a + j + |w| + 4$ steps; the whole source frame is preserved and every rewind and output transition appears in the ledger.
